title: Fix the lost update in the unread counters
problem: increment_unread() and fan_out_unread() pass every single-user test, but under concurrent requests the counters come out too low. Find the read-modify-write pattern and fix both functions so no update can be lost, without changing their behaviour or signatures.
requirements: increment_unread adds exactly 1 and raises LookupError for a non-member, as before
fan_out_unread adds 1 for every member except the sender and returns how many rows changed (0 for an unknown chat)
Each function sends exactly one SQL statement (an UPDATE) besides transaction control
Four threads with their own connections must not lose any increment
contract: increment_unread(conn, chat_id, user_id) -> None; fan_out_unread(conn, chat_id, sender_id) -> int
expectedBehavior: After 4 threads x 50 rounds of increment_unread(1, 20) and fan_out_unread(1, 10), user 20 has 400 unread and user 30 has 200
edgeCases: The sender must not get an unread increment
hints: Conceptual: the bug is the gap between reading the count into Python and writing count + 1 back. Let the database compute the new value from the current one in a single statement.
Specific: SET col = col + 1 in the UPDATE itself. Without the SELECT, how do you know whether a member existed? Look at what the cursor tells you after an UPDATE (sqlite3 docs, Cursor.rowcount).

Implementation: cur = conn.execute('UPDATE chat_members SET unread_count = unread_count + 1 WHERE ...', params); conn.commit(); then use cur.rowcount. For the fan-out, put the 'not the sender' condition into the WHERE clause.
evaluation: No SELECT before the UPDATE in either function
You can explain why the starter loses updates even though SQLite is serializable
